chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from ‘Ali ibn Ibrāhīm, from Ibrāhīm ibn Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Ḥammād al-Anṣārī, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:

When one of you takes clay from the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him), let him say: O Allāh! I ask You through the right of the angel who picked it, and the Messenger who appointed it, and the Successor who is lying within it, to make it a cure from every disease, such and such, and he mentions that disease.

key_terms.طِينُ قَبْرِ الْحُسَيْنِ: Clay from the grave of al-Husayn

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for healing when taking clay from the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia practice of using *turbah* (clay) from Karbala as a medium for *shifa* (healing), grounding the supplication in the cosmic hierarchy of the Prophet, the Angel, and the Imām. By invoking the 'right' (*haqq*) of these figures, the du‘ā emphasizes the metaphysical authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting the Shia belief in their intercessory role and the sanctity of their physical remains. This practice underscores the tangible connection between the believer and the Imām, transforming a simple act of collection into a spiritually potent ritual of healing.
